title: Embeddings client: resilient async streaming, resumable cursors, and structured error surface
creator: Leah Chen
description: Background: Customers running large-scale semantic search and reranking are hitting two classes of issues with the current Embeddings client: long-tail latency spikes during bulk ingestion, and brittle client-side pagination on partial failures. Aim: deliver a resilient, async-first Embeddings SDK surface (Python + TS) that supports streaming responses with backpressure, resumable pagination cursors, and a small set of well-documented structured error types for deterministic retry logic. Scope: (1) Python async iterator + sync wrapper, (2) TypeScript AsyncIterable + typed response envelopes, (3) a resumable cursor token format (opaque + versioned) and server compatibility checks, (4) mapping of transient vs. permanent errors (EmbTransientError, EmbQuotaError, EmbValidationError) and canonical retry semantics, (5) adaptive batching heuristics to reduce per-token latency for short documents, (6) SDK-level metrics and hooks for tracing and cost attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK exposes async iterator: EmbeddingsClient.stream_embeddings(...) that yields typed EmbeddingRecord objects and supports client-side cancellation/backpressure.
TypeScript SDK exposes AsyncIterable with identical semantics and exported types for response envelopes and error discriminants.
Server emits stable resumable_cursor tokens; SDK can recover from mid-page failures using the cursor and resume without duplicate embeddings when idempotency key is provided.
Structured error surface documented: three top-level error classes and clear recommended retry windows (immediate retry, exponential backoff, abort).
Benchmarks: end-to-end bulk ingest latency 95th percentile reduced by >=20% for mixed short/long doc workloads compared to baseline client.
Automated test coverage for pagination resume, transient failure simulation, and exponential-backoff behavior in CI.
Docs and migration guide published under Console SDK docs with code samples for Python/TS.
No breaking changes to existing sync-only endpoint; new streaming APIs are additive and opt-in via new method names.
Runtime rollout gated behind feature flag for hosted customers and integration test against staging runtime-1.23.
Security review: storage of resumable cursor does not leak PII and tokens are short-lived and versioned.
technical_notes: Resumable cursor format: base64(JSON({v:2, model: 'embed-*-v1', seq: <int>, checksum: <sha256>})) to allow future server-side compatibility checks.
Backpressure: implement asyncio.Queue with configurable maxsize on Python side; underlying HTTP client should support chunked streaming and pause/resume.
Typed responses: Python dataclasses + pydantic models for EmbeddingRecord {id, vector, metadata, token_count, provenance}, TS types use generics and discriminated unions for errors.
Idempotency: SDK supplies per-request idempotency_key header when resuming mid-stream to avoid duplicates; server honors dedupe window configurable by deployment.
Adaptive batching: client-side heuristic that groups requests up to N tokens or M documents, whichever first; default tuned from benchmarking traces (N=4096 tokens, M=32 docs).
Retry map: HTTP 502/503/504 -> EmbTransientError (retry with jittered exponential backoff), 429 -> EmbQuotaError (respect Retry-After), 400/422 -> EmbValidationError (do not retry).
Metrics exported: embeddings.request.latency (histogram), embeddings.chunk.size, embeddings.retry.count, embeddings.resume.count; SDK exposes hooks for Redwood Console tracing.
Compatibility: keep existing paginated REST endpoints unchanged; implement streaming/pagination resume as an optional query param `stream=true&resumable=true`.
Performance safety: add circuit-breaker in SDK to fail fast when sustained error rate > 10% for 60s to avoid cascading retries.
Cross-language parity: ensure parity tests between Python and TS via shared golden test corpus (see test_plan links).

test_plan: Unit tests: cursor encode/decode, error mapping, idempotency header behavior.
Integration: end-to-end against staging runtime with synthetic corpus (small/large docs), validate resume correctness and no-duplicates.
Load tests: 10k concurrent streaming clients to measure resume and backpressure stability; compare P95 before/after.
Golden tests: parity between Python and TS outputs for identical request sequences; inject transient failures and assert deterministic resume semantics.
Security tests: ensure cursors expire and cannot be used across accounts; pen-test cursor decoding path.
perf_results: Spike results (2026-03-06): short-doc workload (median doc length=28 tokens): baseline 95p=1.2s -> prototype streaming 95p=0.98s (-18%), p50 unchanged.
Batching tuning (2026-03-09): adaptive heuristic reduced token overage by 12% on mixed workloads, improving throughput by ~7%.
Resume overhead measured: resuming from mid-page added avg 42ms per resume vs full page re-request 210ms; dedupe window avoided duplicates in 99.9% test runs.
